'''''Satureja montana''''' ('''winter savory''' or '''mountain savory'''), is a perennial, semi-evergreen [[herb]] in the family [[Lamiaceae]], native to warm temperate regions of southern [[Europe]], the [[Mediterranean]], and [[Africa]]. It has dark green leaves and summer flowers ranging from pale lavender, or pink to white. The closely related [[summer savory]] (''Satureja hortensis'' L.) is an annual plant.

==Description==
It grows to between {{convert|4|and|16|in|cm|-1|abbr=on|order=flip}} tall.<ref name=botany/><ref name="Linford"/> The leathery,<ref name="Linford"/> dark green<ref name=rhs>{{cite web|title=Satureja montana winter savory|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16484/i-Satureja-montana-i/Details|publisher=rhs.org.u|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite, oval-lanceolate or needle-like,<ref name=Allinone>Bob Beckstrom, Karan Davis Cutler, Kathleen Fisher, Phillip Giroux, Judy Glattstein, Michael MacCaskey, Bill Marken, Charlie Nardozzi, Sally Roth, Marcia Tatroe, Lance Walheim and Ann Whitman {{google books|qW7Zo17oircC|Gardening All-in-One For Dummies|page=674}}</ref> 1–2 cm long and 5 mm broad. The [[flower]]s appear in summer,<ref name=Allinone/> between July and October,<ref name=pfaf/> and range from pale lavender or pink to white.<ref name="Linford"/><ref name="herbs">{{cite web|title=Savory Satureja hortensis / Satureja montana|url=http://www.herbs2000.com/herbs/herbs_savory.htm|publisher=herbs2000.com|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> The flowers are smaller than summer savoury flowers.<ref name=Peter/> It contains [[carvacrol]],<ref name="herbs"/> a [[monoterpenoid]] [[phenol]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Vladić|first1=Jelena|last2=Zeković|first2=Zoran|last3=Jokić|first3=Stela|last4=Svilović|first4=Sandra|last5=Kovačević|first5=Strahinja|last6=Vidović|first6=Senka|title=Winter savory: Supercritical carbon dioxide extraction and mathematical modeling of extraction process|journal=The Journal of Supercritical Fluids|date=November 2016|volume=117|pages=89–97|doi=10.1016/j.supflu.2016.05.027}}</ref>

The herb was first published by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his book [[Species Plantarum]] on page 568 in 1753.<ref name="plantlist">{{cite web|title=Satureja montana L. is an accepted name|url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-185794|publisher=theplantlist.org|access-date=29 September 2017|date=23 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lamiaceae Satureja montana L.|url=https://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=457736-1|publisher=ipni.org|access-date=29 September 2017}}</ref> The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''montana'' refers to mountains or coming from mountains,<ref>Archibald William Smith {{google books|ahNMkgoNJ7IC|A Gardener's Handbook of Plant Names: Their Meanings and Origins|page=239}}</ref> leading to the common name 'mountain savory'.<ref name="Linford"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Satureja montana'' is [[native plant|native]] to [[temperate]] areas between Europe,<ref name=rhs/> the Mediterranean,<ref name=botany>{{cite web|last1=Gutzerová|first1=Naděžda|title=SATUREJA MONTANA L. – saturejka horská|url=https://botany.cz/cs/satureja-montana/|website=botany.cz|access-date=14 January 2015}}</ref> and Africa.<ref name="pfaf">{{cite web|title=Satureja montana - L.|url=https://pfaf.org/User/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Satureja+montana|publisher=pfaf.org|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref>
It has been naturalised in [[Great Britain]].<ref name="pfaf"/> It can be found growing in old walls, on dry banks and rocks on hillsides,<ref name="pfaf"/> or rocky mountain slopes,<ref name="Linford">{{cite book|last1=Linford|first1=Jenny|title=A concise guide to herbs|date=2010|publisher=Parragon|location=Bath|isbn=9781405487993|page=210}}</ref> usually on [[calcareous]]<ref name="pfaf"/> or [[alkaline]] soils.<ref name=rhs/>

==Cultivation and uses==
There is evidence of its use about 2000 years ago by the ancient [[Ancient Rome|Romans]] and Greeks.<ref name="Linford"/>

Winter savory is easy to grow and can be used as a culinary [[herb garden]] edging plant.<ref name="Linford" /> It requires six hours of sun per day and well-draining soil.<ref name=Goddard>Sandra-Jane Goddard {{google books|6j6sBwAAQBAJ|What Mary Knew|page=241}}</ref> In temperate climates it becomes dormant in winter, putting out leaves on the bare stems in the spring. While dormant, it should not be cut back; stems which appear dead will leaf-out again. Winter savory is hardy and has a low-bunching habit.{{Cn|date=September 2023}}

It is [[Hardiness (plants)|hardy]] to [[USDA]] [[Hardiness zone|Zone 4]]<ref name="Allinone" /> and can be [[Vegetative reproduction|propagated]] from [[softwood]] cuttings.<ref name="rhs" /><ref name="Jane" /> Winter savory is used as a [[companion plant]] for beans, keeping [[bean weevil]]s away, and is also planted with [[rose]]s to reduce [[mildew]] and [[aphid]]s.<ref name="pfaf" /><ref name="Goddard" /><ref>[https://www.stodels.com/index.php/winter-savory winter savory]</ref>

''S. montana'' 'Nana' is a known dwarf cultivar.<ref>{{cite web|title=Creeping Winter Savory 'Nana'|url=http://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/160112/|publisher=davesgarden.com|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref>
''S. montana'' 'Prostrate White' is a small white flowered form.<ref name="BBC">{{cite web|title=Winter savory|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/gardening/plants/plant_finder/plant_pages/831.shtml|publisher=bbc.co.uk|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref>

''S. montana'' is also a [[List of honey plants|honey plant]], with savory honey being a regional product from [[Abruzzo]] in Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Savory Honey - Arca del Gusto |url=https://www.fondazioneslowfood.com/en/ark-of-taste-slow-food/savory-honey/ |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=Slow Food Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Culinary uses==
In cooking, winter savory has a reputation for going very well with both beans and meats,<ref name=Breverton>Terry Breverton {{google books|T4hhBQAAQBAJ|Breverton's Complete Herbal: A Book of Remarkable Plants and Their Uses|page=580}}</ref> very often lighter meats such as [[chicken#Chickens as food|chicken]] or [[domesticated turkey#Turkeys as food|turkey]], and can be used in stuffing. It can also be used in soups and sauces. It has a strong flavour (stronger than summer savory)<ref name="Linford"/><ref name="recipes">{{cite web|title=Savory recipes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/food/savory|publisher=bbc.co.uk|access-date=28 September 2017}}</ref> while uncooked but loses much of its flavour with prolonged cooking. It can be added to [[breadcrumb]]s as a coating for various meats including [[trout]].<ref name=Peter>K. V. Peter (Editor) {{google books|qUaT093PZFAC|Handbook of Herbs and Spices, Volume 2|page=95}}</ref> 
 
==Traditional uses==
[[Image:Satureja montana1.jpg|thumb]]
[[Image:Satureja montana b2.JPG|thumb|closeup image of the flower]]
Winter savory has been purported to have [[antiseptic]], aromatic, [[carminative]], and digestive benefits.<ref name="pfaf"/><ref name=Breverton/> It has also been used as an [[expectorant]], and in the treatment of bee stings<ref name=Jane>Jane Eastoe {{google books|93gyeLatWYAC| Herbs: Inspiration and Practical Advice for Gardeners|page=85}}</ref><ref>Joan Parry Dutton {{google books|XTbQNSIaIoIC|Plants of Colonial Williamsburg: How to Identify 200 of Colonial America's ...|page=153}}</ref><ref>J. Ingle and [[Nicholas Culpeper]] {{google books|w2AUAAAAQAAJ|Pocket companion to Culpeper's herbal, or English physician|page=9}}</ref> or insect bites through the use of a [[poultice]] of the leaves.<ref name=Breverton/> The plant has a stronger action than the closely related summer savory.<ref name=Breverton/>

Taken internally, it is said to be a remedy for [[colic]] and a cure for [[flatulence]], whilst it is also used to treat gastro-enteritis, [[cystitis]], [[nausea]], [[diarrhoea]], bronchial congestion, sore throat and menstrual disorders.<ref name=Breverton/>

Therapeutic-grade oil has been determined to inhibit the growth of ''[[Candida albicans]]''.<ref>Oberg K, Rolling L, Oberg C. in The Journal of the Utah Academy of Sciences, Arts, and Letters. 2005;82:60-72</ref>

The plant is harvested when flowering in the summer and can be used fresh or dried. The essential oil is an ingredient in lotions for the scalp in cases of incipient baldness.<ref name=Goddard/> An ointment made from the plant is used externally to relieve [[arthritic]] joints.<ref name=Breverton/>

In traditional herbal medicine, summer savory was believed to be an [[aphrodisiac]], while winter savory was believed to inhibit sexual desire (an anaphrodisiac).<ref name="herbs"/> French herbalist [[Maurice Mességué]] claimed that savory was 'the herb of happiness'.<ref name=Breverton/>

==Strewing herb==
The Saturejas have been traditionally used to [[Strewing herb|strew]] on the floor since the medieval times, as an aromatic herb that reduce insects.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://plewsgardendesign.co.uk/winter-savory-satureja-montana/ | title=Winter Savory, Satureja montana | date=18 February 2022 }}</ref>
